TRANSCRIPT OF PROCEEDINGS
THE HON CATHERINE HOLMES AC SC, Commissioner
THE ROYAL COMMISSION INTO THE ROBODEBT SCHEME
MONDAY, 7 NOVEMBER 2022 AT 10 AM (AEST)
DAY 8
MR JUSTIN GREGGERY KC, Senior Counsel Assisting
MS DOMINIQUE HOGAN-DORAN SC, for the Commonwealth

COMMISSIONER: Yes, Mr Greggery.
MR GREGGERY: Yes, thank you Commissioner. There is one matter of housekeeping left over
from last week. I can confirm this morning the Solicitors Assisting the Commonwealth, sorry
the Solicitors Assisting the Commission received a letter from the Solicitors Assisting the
Commonwealth which addressed the question of whether witnesses had access to secure
email accounts. It's a lengthy and detailed letter. I understand it doesn't affect any
witnesses today, but that question raised by the Commission last week is being addressed
between the Solicitors, I understand.
COMMISSIONER: Alright. We will want to make that an Exhibit somewhere somehow. Won't
we?
MR GREGGERY: We will in due course, I think, but the two letters you have there relate to
Mr Flavel's evidence. And they will be tendered in - very shortly.
COMMISSIONER: Okay. Thank you. Well, you won't lose sight of wanting to get that letter
on the record or does it not need to be on the record?
MR GREGGERY: Not at this point, no.
COMMISSIONER: Okay. Thank you.
MR GREGGERY: Matthew Flavel is the next witness for today. And he's in a position to be
sworn.
COMMISSIONER: Okay. It is Mr Flavel is it, not Flavell? Flavel. Okay. Thank you. Swear Mr
Flavel.
ASSOCIATE: Do you swear by Almighty God that the evidence you will give will be the truth,
the whole truth and nothing but the truth?
MR FLAVEL: I do.
ASSOCIATE: Thank you.
<MATTHEW JAMES FLAVEL, SWORN
<EXAMINATION BY MR GREGGERY KC
COMMISSIONER: Yes, Mr Greggery.
MR GREGGERY: Yes, thank you, Commissioner. Your full name is Matthew James Flavel?
MR FLAVEL: That's correct.

MR GREGGERY: And your current position is the Deputy Secretary within the Department of
Social Services?
MR FLAVEL: That's correct.
MR GREGGERY: Particularly in Social Security?
MR FLAVEL: That's right.
MR GREGGERY: How long have you held that position?
MR FLAVEL: I came into that position on 9 November 2020.
MR GREGGERY: You received a - or, rather, NTG-0010 was a notice to give a statement and
produce documents addressed to the proper officer of the Department of Social Services
dated 11 October 2022. Are you familiar with that notice?
MR FLAVEL: Yes, I am.
MR GREGGERY: And you produced a statement in response as the proper officer, dated 19
October 2022?
MR FLAVEL: That's right.
MR GREGGERY: Alright. In addition to that notice and your statement, there were two other
notices addressed to the proper officer of the Department of Social Services, NTG-0002 and
NTG-0003, and responses were provided by the Department to both of those notices as well
and you are familiar with those?
MR FLAVEL: I am familiar with those, yes.
MR GREGGERY: Commissioner, I tender the documents in the index relating to Mr Flavel,
Exhibits 831 through to 843.
COMMISSIONER: Alright. Documents 831 to 843 are admitted as Exhibits with those
numbers as per the schedule. Thank you.
<EXHIBITS 831 TO 843 AS PER THE SCHEDULE
MR GREGGERY: And for completeness, Commissioner, the two letters which your associate
placed before you are marked on the Exhibit list as 837A and 837B.
COMMISSIONER: Thank you.
<EXHIBITS 837A AND 837B LETTERS

MR GREGGERY: Dated 20 October and 23 October 2022 respectively. Mr Flavel, just before
we go - - -
COMMISSIONER: Flavel. Flavel.
MR GREGGERY: Mr Flavel, just before - I started off so well - Mr Flavel, just before we go
into the detail of your statement, were you provided with letters by the Solicitors assisting
the Commonwealth dated 22 October 2022 and 23 October 2022 in respect of your
statement? I will provide you with a hard copy so that you can have a look at those.
MR FLAVEL: Yes, I recall these documents.
MR GREGGERY: Alright. Might I have one moment? And did you make some changes to your
statements in response to those documents?
MR FLAVEL: I don't recall making changes to it. I think, from memory, it caused me to make
some additional - to look for some additional documents.
MR GREGGERY: The - and do you recall that the - a letter was provided by your instructors, I
think, responding to the - your search for further documents dated 28 October 2022? Do
you recall that?
MR FLAVEL: I recall that document, yes.
MR GREGGERY: Okay. I will arrange for a hard copy to be presented and tendered as 837C,
Commissioner.
COMMISSIONER: And I'm sorry, what was the last thing you said? 837C?
MR GREGGERY: Yes.
COMMISSIONER: Thank you. That’s admitted.
<EXHIBIT 837C LETTER DATED 28/10/2022
MR GREGGERY: Mr Flavel, you identify your professional experience from the point you
joined the Department in January 2020 as the Group Manager of the Market Capability
Group in the Disability and Carers Stream. Were you in a different Department before that
point in time?
MR FLAVEL: Yes, from around - testing my memory, I think from late 2003 through to 2020 I
was, I was in the Treasury, the Federal Treasury.
MR GREGGERY: And what position did you hold there when you - - -
MR FLAVEL: Various positions over the course of that 16 years, all at the Senior Executive

MR GREGGERY: The most recent of those?
MR FLAVEL: Was as the Chief Operating Officer or the Deputy Secretary Corporate Services.
MR GREGGERY: Did you have any involvement when you were with the Treasury
Department in respect of what became the Robodebt Scheme or what was the Robodebt
Scheme?
MR FLAVEL: No, I didn't. I think from the - I was the - I forget the title but the Division Head
of the Budget Policy Division in Treasury for the 2015-16, '16/17 and '17/18 budgets. That
involved a whole lot of coordination of budget material, so I would have been broadly aware
of some of the measures that were under consideration, but nothing more than sort of at
arm's length. The role there was much more of whole of budget strategy, fiscal strategy
rather than burrowing down into the details of individual measures.
MR GREGGERY: Alright. In preparing your statement as the proper officer for the
Department of Social Services in response to NTG-0010, is it the case that because you only
joined the Department in 2020, your information has been obtained from, essentially, a
document review?
MR FLAVEL: That's correct, yes
MR GREGGERY: And some conversations with other people who may have been present
during the relevant periods?
MR FLAVEL: Yes, through the identification of certain people who may have been around at
the time, who were still in the Department, making some inquiries of them.
MR GREGGERY: As I read your statement, you don't detail what information came from
what person in respect of the response to your statement? It's presented in a summary
form, as it were. Are you able now to identify what information came from what person or
just broadly - - -
MR FLAVEL: I think what I would say is that the information - each of the people that I made
contact with, which was via email, came back and said that they did not have anything
further to add. So, in effect, my response in the witness statement is the summation of all
the documents that were located as part of the search.
MR GREGGERY: Alright. In terms of preparing a review of documents, what was the process
by which you ascertained relevant documents in response to the notice?
MR FLAVEL: So it was a fairly comprehensive search process undertaken by a - an area set
up in the Department to undertake that purpose. It involved looking at various data bases or
sources of information. So things like the Parliamentary document management system,
other repositories of the Department using identified search criteria. So things like online

put in NTG-0010, running some further search terms and also cross - I should call it
cross-checking or doing further identification based on the emails of particular individuals in
senior positions who were in the Department of Social Services at the time.
MR GREGGERY: Can you confirm whether you not you had access to secure email accounts
as part of those search processes or those conducting the search had access to the secure
email accounts?
MR FLAVEL: I can't say with certainty it was accessing secure email accounts.
MR GREGGERY: Did you take any steps to ensure the searches were conducted of secure
email accounts?
MR FLAVEL: The information I was given was a search of email accounts. I don't think it was
specific to whether it was secure email or other email.
MR FLAVEL: Right. And as I read an electronic copy of 837C, that's the letter in response by
Solicitors Assisting the Commonwealth, the persons that you spoke to within the document
are as follows: Andrew Whitecross; Emmakate McGuirk; Katherine Paton, one T; Lydia Ross;
Anita Davis; James Kemp; Alfred Opoku, O-p-o-k-u; Paul Dowling and Diana Lindenmayer.
MR FLAVEL: That's correct, yes.
COMMISSIONER: So, essentially, the statement we got from you may be based on some
relatively small proportion of the actual DHS material, for all you know?
MR FLAVEL: The DSS material, Commissioner?
COMMISSIONER: Sorry, DSS material.
MR FLAVEL: Well, I think it involved the collation of around 31,000 documents, I think, in the
first instance. So that, I think, is a reasonably comprehensive set of documents from which
to then do a more detailed search.
COMMISSIONER: It's possibly excluding any held as secure emails though?
MR FLAVEL: That may be the case, but, as I said, I'm not personally aware of the specific way
in which the issue of secure emails was handled by those undertaking the searches.
COMMISSIONER: Well, to state the obvious, you don't know what you didn't see?
MR FLAVEL: Correct, yes.
COMMISSIONER: Okay, thanks.
MR GREGGERY: Did you see any emails from secure email accounts of either Serena Wilson

MR FLAVEL: I can't recall, actually.
MR GREGGERY: And as you say in your statement at paragraph 17, what follows from what
you have elaborated on here is that you're aware your responses may not provide the Royal
Commission with answers to all the questions in the notice to give a statement?
MR FLAVEL: Yes, that's right.
MR GREGGERY: One of the requirements to provide a statement was to refer to documents
already produced to the Royal Commission by their document identification number, and
attach to your statement a list and copies of all documents referred to that have not been
produced to the Royal Commission. I don't see any reference in your statement to a
reference to relevant documents already provided to the Royal Commission by their
document identification number. Can you explain that?
MR FLAVEL: Sorry, can you repeat the question?
MR GREGGERY: Your statement doesn't refer to relevant documents already provided to the
Royal Commission by their document identification number, which was a requirement of
the request for a statement. Are you able to identify why that was not done?
MR FLAVEL: Sorry, I'm not able to identify, no.
MR GREGGERY: Did you discuss that requirement of the notice with the solicitor who
assisted to you provide your statement?
MR FLAVEL: To be honest, I don't think it came up during the discussions I had in the
preparation of my statement.
MR GREGGERY: Was your statement largely prepared on your own initiative?
MR FLAVEL: It was with the assistance of the people conducting the searches.
MR GREGGERY: Within the Department?
MR FLAVEL: Yes, that's right.
MR GREGGERY: Alright. And then provided to the Australian Government Solicitor?
MR FLAVEL: That's correct.
COMMISSIONER: You see, it's not very helpful because you make assertions about a state of
affairs but you give no supporting documentation, so there's no way of the Commission
looking at what you were looking at to see why you say things. Was that not obvious for you
as you prepared this, that you would make an assertion, for example, that the Department

obtained internal policy and legal advice concerning the proposed use of the income
averaging but provide no document reference at all. So one can only guess why you say it.
MR FLAVEL: I understand the point you're making. I was provided with assistance in
preparing it, and that issue about the provision of the supporting documents did not come
up in the preparation of my statement. I have, however, looked at all of the documents that
were used in the construction of that statement.
COMMISSIONER: Well, that's great for you but we are never going to know what they were.
It just - I find it really hard to understand how you could think that this would be useful to
ask us basically to take your word, that's what the documents say about various points,
without giving the Commission any opportunity to look for itself.
MR FLAVEL: Commissioner, with apologies, I relied on others in terms of the preparation of
the statement. The fact that the documents that supported the contentions are made were
not being made available - actually was not known to me. I had assumed that that would be
the case.
COMMISSIONER: Look, they might be available, but we have hundreds of thousands of
documents, so we just have no means of working out which ones they were. That's the
greater problem. And I - I can't understand why somebody as obviously as intelligent as
yourself didn't spot it as an issue?
MR FLAVEL: It may just reflect my lack of experience with the Royal Commission process in
terms of how the provision of documents and support would be provided to the
Commission.
COMMISSIONER: Who helped you?
MR FLAVEL: We had our own internal legal area and an external provider providing the
assistance.
COMMISSIONER: Alright. I will leave it there. Back to you, Mr Greggery.
MR GREGGERY: Thank you, Commissioner. You may have recalled Mr Flavel that in the letter
20 October 2022, Exhibit 837A, specific attention was drawn to this in the paragraph that
said:
"In addition, we note that in the response, Mr Flavel indicates that he has reviewed various
materials to inform himself about the matters to which he is responding. In most cases, the
response does not make clear what that material is, nor does it indicate whether the
material will be produced to the Royal Commission. For the avoidance of doubt the Royal
Commission requires Mr Flavel, pursuant to the notice, to produce those materials subject to
any relevant privileges and/or immunities.”
Do you recall that in the letter?

MR FLAVEL: I recall that, yes.
MR GREGGERY: What happened after that letter, in terms of a response by you?
MR FLAVEL: I don't think I provided an additional response after that.
COMMISSIONER: Were you not taking the Royal Commission seriously? I just don't
understand this.
MR FLAVEL: No, I - I don't want to give that impression, Commissioner. I was taking it very
seriously. It's just the actual process, I had been led to believe that those documents would
have been provided in support of my statement. I take the point that they may not, in
amongst a very large number of documents, have been specifically identified.
MR GREGGERY: Well, Mr Flavel, the importance the specifically identifying the documents
was reiterated in the letter of 23 October 2022, 837B. Which says that:
"The Royal Commission required production by 12 pm, Friday, 21 October 2022 of the
material Mr Flavel relied on to prepare the response. However, we do not believe that we
have received that material. The Royal Commission requires production of the material,
together with the names of any staff Mr Flavel consulted in relation to the preparation of the
response by way of an updated response to the notice.”
And a deadline of 5 pm, Monday, 24 October 2022 was given. The extent of the response, I
gather, was contained in the letter now Exhibit 837C, 28 October 2022.
MR FLAVEL: I recall that was a letter that had the names of the people I had spoken to.
MR GREGGERY: Yes.
MR FLAVEL: And some further information about the searches.
MR GREGGERY: Yes. For example, you refer in paragraph 21 of your statement to various
administrative arrangements orders that were in force during the relevant time. Those are
not identified with any specificity in your statement?
MR FLAVEL: That's right. Although the - the administrative arrangements orders are public
documents on the website of the - of the Australian Parliament.
MR GREGGERY: We can find those for ourselves?
MR FLAVEL: Correct, yes.
MR GREGGERY: Yes. What about the Instruments of Delegation you refer to at paragraph
26?

MR GREGGERY: And where would we find those, if we went looking?
MR FLAVEL: I think on the Federal Register of Legislative Instruments, but I would need to
check that.
MR GREGGERY: And then in paragraph 42, you say this:
"From my review of documents I understand the PAYG manual compliance intervention as
defined in the NTG comprised..."
Two stages, it would seem. Are you able to identify now what those documents were? Are
they publicly available documents as well?
MR FLAVEL: The 42(b) is a statement around the material that was made available in the
2015-2016 Budget, I think. The Strengthening and Integrity of the Welfare Payments Budget
Measure was outlined there.
MR GREGGERY: Right. What about (a)?
MR FLAVEL: I don't think that (a) would have been a public document, from memory.
MR GREGGERY: In terms of paragraph 43 just below it, again, you use the phrase, "From my
review of documents being implemented by the agency" and you refer to two measures.
Are they publicly available budget measures, are they?
MR FLAVEL: Yes, those were the names by which they were used in the Mid-Year Economic
and Fiscal Outlook, the following Mid-Year Economic and Fiscal Outlook.
MR GREGGERY: Similarly, at paragraph 44, again, you refer to the "the material I've referred
to date." Paragraph (a) refers to budget measures which I understand you have identified
above and also described as new policy proposals. (B) refers to:
"The Department had input into the proposal to use income averaging...”
I pause there. What documents are you referring to by the Department's input or which
might evidence the Department's input in the proposal to use income averaging?
MR FLAVEL: Some of the documents that have already been referred to in evidence,
including around the interactions between then DHS and DSS in relation to the development
of that particular proposal in the latter part of 2015 - 2014 and early 2015.
MR GREGGERY: You can appreciate why it's significant, then, to identify with specific
document identification reference documents which have already been produced to the
Commission, if that's what you are referring to?

MR GREGGERY: You appreciate that in order to understand your statement, we have to go
through a very lengthy oral process now, given the limited response to the letters of 20 and
23 October?
MR FLAVEL: (Inaudible)
MR GREGGERY: How was it that you were selected as the proper officer to respond to the
notice, given that you weren't involved in the Department at the time and your information
is essentially limited to documents which you have been referred to by others but not
specifically identified?
MR FLAVEL: I think it was ultimately a decision of the Secretary of the Department, taking
into account that the matters under consideration were quite some time ago. So, you know,
around eight years. All of the senior people involved through that period no longer are in
roles. In fact, you know, very - very few senior people from that time still being in the
Department. Given that the matter is under the broad policy area under investigation sits
within my remit, that as the most senior person responsible, that I should be the proper
officer for the response.
MR GREGGERY: One of the names that was referred to in the letter of 28 October 2022,
which I read out, was Andrew Whitecross. Was he still in the Department?
MR FLAVEL: Is he still in the Department? He is an officer of the Department, but he's
actually been in a couple of other roles outside of the Department over the past couple of
years.
MR GREGGERY: So is he in the Department now?
MR FLAVEL: So I think formally he is a Senior Executive Service Officer of the Department on
secondment to - he was at the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission, sorry, at the
Australian Institute of Family Studies and I think has also been at the NDIS Quality and
Safeguards Commission.
MR GREGGERY: In your review of documents, did you identify that he was involved at a
relatively high level in obtaining or being informed of legal advice and policy advice in
November and December 2014?
MR FLAVEL: My recollection is that he was a branch manager at that time. So a Senior
Executive Service Officer, level 1. So he would have had a Senior Executive Service level 2
and 3 or a Deputy Secretary and Secretary above him at that time. My recollection is that he
was also not in that role for the entirety of the period.
COMMISSIONER: Well, he might have had a clue about what was going on and what to look
for, Mr Flavel?

MR FLAVEL: Yes, and I did make contact. He was listed as one of the people I made contact
within the preparation of my statement.
COMMISSIONER: Is there any burning reason he couldn't have undertaken this activity of
taking responsibility for identifying what mattered?
MR FLAVEL: It may come down to a technicality. He is an officer of the Department, but he
is actually not in the Department. He is actually on secondment. And I guess that a decision
was taken that it might be unusual to have somebody who was not particularly senior at the
time giving a broad sweep of a whole range of questions and also being on secondment to
another agency.
MR GREGGERY: Well, there's a difference, you would appreciate, between someone who is
conducting a document review such as yourself and someone who has actual knowledge of
relevant events. You appreciate the distinction.
MR FLAVEL: I appreciate the distinction, noting I did speak with him, or I did make contact
with him, rather, as part of my - part of my witness - part of my statement preparation.
COMMISSIONER: Did you have a chat about the advice he got in 2014?
MR FLAVEL: No, it was all via email.
COMMISSIONER: Any discussion via email about the 2014 advice and what it actually said?
MR FLAVEL: I don't think that he had, from memory, anything further to add, other than to
note that the advice which has already been tendered in evidence, that he didn't have
anything further to add to that.
COMMISSIONER: What he did with it? He didn't tell you that?
MR FLAVEL: No, he didn't.
MR GREGGERY: When you say he didn't have anything further to add, what did you provide
him with to consider and potentially add to?
MR FLAVEL: I asked for a review of emails, and he had provided copies of emails which were
already on our files of the interactions which he had over the issue around the legal advice
in the run-up to the development of the proposal
MR GREGGERY: Do you mean that you asked him to review his own email accounts?
MR FLAVEL: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: That is, without specifying whether it included a secure email account?

MR FLAVEL: As I have said earlier, I can't comment any further on the secure email element,
but I did ask for a review to ensure we had all relevant documents.
MR GREGGERY: And, but specifically in respect of Mr Whitecross, did you ask him
specifically about his emails or did you present him with what had been prepared to you?
MR FLAVEL: It was a general request and included requesting officers to check their own
emails for any emails or evidence that may be relevant, given the Terms of Reference for
the Commission.
MR GREGGERY: Sorry, so it was an email from you to various persons, all at once?
MR FLAVEL: No, individually.
MR GREGGERY: Which asked them to undertake a search of their own email accounts or
emails for what might be relevant to the terms of the Commission?
MR FLAVEL: I think relevant to the preparation of notice to give 0010, actually.
MR GREGGERY: So how did you frame that request to each of the recipients?
MR FLAVEL: Pretty much as we have discussed here, it was an email asking them to do it a
review or to advise of any other information which may be relevant
MR GREGGERY: Yes, but the question of "other information which may be relevant"
suggests they were given some information which may be relevant and asked to add to it.
Did that occur?
MR FLAVEL: No, it was the - I - I'm almost certain it was the questions that were contained in
NTG-0010.
MR GREGGERY: I see. So the request either attached NTG-0010 or a summarised version of
questions from NTG-0010 and asked specific people to check their own emails to see what
they might have.
MR FLAVEL: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: And everyone to whom you sent that request replied that they didn't have
anything to add?
MR FLAVEL: Nothing to add or no other information that they found relevant.
MR GREGGERY: Do you appreciate that there might be a deficiency in that response by
asking people who might have been involved with the Robodebt Scheme, which ended up
attracting some adverse attention, to conduct their own self-assessment of what might be
relevant?

MR FLAVEL: It was as an additional layer as opposed to of itself being the way to source
documents. In other words, searches had already been conducted in the preparation of my
statement. It was an additional layer, if you will, designed to ensure that we had made
maximum inquiries.
MR GREGGERY: But the additional layer really was just your request and their response,
without you being able to satisfy yourself that anything had actually happened in response
to your request?
MR FLAVEL: It was a way of ensuring that, given the amount of time that elapsed, that if
there happened to be any other documents that they felt fitted within the notice, they
could provide those.
MR GREGGERY: But as I understand it, they weren't given any documents at all. They were
just given a list of questions?
MR FLAVEL: That's right, yes.
MR GREGGERY: So the reference to any other documents doesn't have any context to this?
MR FLAVEL: Any documents, I think.
MR GREGGERY: So they didn't know what had been prepared by those conducting the
searches to assist you with your statement; correct?
MR FLAVEL: That's correct, yes.
MR GREGGERY: And, you know, uniformly every single person replied and said they couldn't
locate anything?
MR FLAVEL: That's not correct. I think Mr Whitecross did produce a number of emails.
MR GREGGERY: Is he the only person who produced emails?
MR FLAVEL: I am just trying to remember. I think possibly Emmakate McGuirk would have
been the other one.
MR GREGGERY: And you no doubt have these emails?
MR FLAVEL: I think that they have been the subject of discussions in evidence given last
week, yes.
MR GREGGERY: I'm not interested in trying to unravel what - conduct a cross-referencing
exercise there. I'm just identifying you received emails which attached emails from those
two persons?

MR GREGGERY: And your review of those emails is to the effect that they didn't add to what
you were already told?
MR FLAVEL: That's correct.
MR GREGGERY: Did any other person reply with emails?
MR FLAVEL: Not that I recall, no. Most of the other people who replied may have been in
the area, you know, that was responsible for debt and integrity or similar issues over a
lengthy period.
MR GREGGERY: And how were they identified as being potentially relevant?
MR FLAVEL: Through a review of organisational charts over the period.
MR GREGGERY: That is they were identified as holding relevant positions during the period
which would be responsive to questions in the notice?
MR FLAVEL: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: But were unable to or did not produce any emails from the relevant period?
MR FLAVEL: That's correct.
MR GREGGERY: Did that strike you as odd?
MR FLAVEL: Well, in some cases their involvement - their time in role may have been well
after, you know, the period of sort of 2014/15. So not necessarily surprising.
MR GREGGERY: And for the other cases?
MR FLAVEL: I think that in the case of Ms McGuirk and Mr Whitecross, it confirmed
documents which we had already sourced for the preparation of my statement.
MR GREGGERY: Of the category of respondees who were in positions at the relevant time
but did not produce any documents, did that strike you as odd?
MR FLAVEL: Those who were not in?
MR GREGGERY: Yes.
MR FLAVEL: No, it did not strike me as odd.
MR GREGGERY: So we can read for ourselves your statement about legislative schemes,
administrative orders, delegations and the like and accept you or someone assisting you has

MR FLAVEL: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: If we go to paragraph 29(a) of your statement, and 29(b), you were asked
this question at question 3 of the notice:
"Describe the governance arrangements established or applied by the Department for the
management and/or oversight of the planning design development (including testing,
establishment and implementation each of PAYG manual compliance intervention and OCI
programs.)”
You refer here to a Bilateral Management Arrangement between the Department of Social
Services and the Department of Human Services, described as "the agency", with an
effective date of 22 October 2014, varied March '16 and replaced on April 2018 and another
Payment Assurance Arrangement with the same commencement date. If we go, then, to
paragraph 29 - sorry, 30. Thank you. You say this, that you are:
"...unable to comment on the degree to which the Bilateral Management Arrangement or
the payment assurance service arrangement was adhered to in respect of the first two
iterations of the Robodebt Scheme.”
Why were you unable to ascertain whether they were adhered to?
MR FLAVEL: So I said I'm unable to comment on the degree to which they were adhered to.
MR GREGGERY: Yes. Why is that?
MR FLAVEL: Because there's no direct link between the measures announced, commonly
known as the sort of Robodebt, and those two documents.
MR GREGGERY: What do you mean "no direct link"? I don't understand.
MR FLAVEL: Well, those documents are really about establishing a framework for explaining
the - you know, some of the general governance arrangements that exist between the DSS
and then DHS, now Services Australia.
MR GREGGERY: Yes, I understand that. But, plainly, they regulate the relationship between
the Department of Social Services and the Department of Human Services in many respects,
including of the Robodebt Scheme; correct?
MR FLAVEL: They establish a general framework for - for the conduct of activities and
include outlining the who does what.
MR GREGGERY: And that arrangement would have applied to the Robodebt Scheme
wouldn't it? It would have fallen underneath this arrangement?

MR GREGGERY: And that's why you have included it, because it was relevant governance
structure in respect of the early stages of the Robodebt Scheme?
